title: Adaptive threshold controller for steady-state batching and graceful backpressure
creator: Maya Chen
description: Under sustained high QPS some hosts observe repeated microburst-induced OOM spikes and tail-latency climbs. Current static microbatch thresholds and simple headroom checks cause either wasteful conservative shedding or late, disruptive evictions of KV cache. This ticket implements an adaptive threshold controller that adjusts micro-batch admission and soft backpressure signals based on predictive GPU headroom estimates and workload characteristics, with explicit coordination with KV eviction priority and tenant fairness windows.
rationale: Static thresholds don't generalize across tenants and model sequence distributions. We need a controller that (1) reduces false-positive shedding when transient bursts occur, (2) proactively throttles admission before hard memory pressure, and (3) coordinates with KV eviction to avoid evicting hot prefixes aggressively. The approach should be lightweight, observable, and safe to roll out as a runtime flag.
design_notes: High-level algorithm: (a) continuous EWMA of per-host memory utilization with two time constants (fast for microbursts, slow for trend); (b) an adaptive threshold computed as headroom_target = baseline_headroom + alpha * stddev(windowed_util) where alpha decays with load; (c) PID-like correction to microbatch size ceiling and admission rate multiplier; (d) soft backpressure states: green/yellow/red mapped to admission multipliers [1.0, 0.6-0.8, 0.2-0.5] and preferred eviction aggressiveness; (e) KV eviction policy ties into backpressure: in yellow, prefer cold-prefix eviction with min-hot-score; in red, allow aggressive slab reclaim while preserving top-k hot prefixes for pinned sessions; (f) fairness: per-tenant moving-window budget ensures a noisy tenant cannot starve others — controller subtracts a tenant-specific penalty factor derived from recent CPU/GPU share and request success ratio; (g) safety: enforce absolute hard floor on microbatch size (>=1), and circuit-breaker disabling adaptive controller if observed error rate increases by >5% within 1m after change.
implementation_plan: Prototype controller in the local runtime agent (C++) with feature flag runtime.adaptive_batching.v1
Add metrics: host_memory_util_fast, host_memory_util_slow, adaptive_threshold, admission_multiplier, backpressure_state, kv_eviction_priority, tenant_penalty_factor
Add tests: unit tests for EWMA and PID logic, integration test with mem-pressure generator container to validate transitions
Instrument canary fleet (10 hosts) with shadow rollout for 48h and collect crash/oom/latency/regression metrics
Iterate tuning knobs (alpha, time constants, multipliers) and produce recommended defaults for GA
Gradual rollout across Dedicated clusters with telemetry gating and rollback runbook
acceptance_criteria: No increase in 95th token-latency above 5% on canary compared to baseline under production-matched load
OOM count on canary fleet reduced by >= 60% for sustained high QPS scenarios in the experiment
KV cache hit-rate degradation <= 3% or explained by reduced total tokens served (i.e., lower cost)
Backpressure state and admission_multiplier exposed in Console per-host and per-tenant dashboards
Fail-safe circuit-breaker and rollout flag validated in chaos test (forced false positives)
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Design walkthrough with runtime and infra completed; consensus on EWMA + PID hybrid approach.

2026-03-08: Added telemetry hooks and Grafana panels for headroom_target and backpressure_state. Observed noisy tenants causing frequent yellow transitions during internal test load.
2026-03-11: Introduced tenant_penalty_factor to damp noisy tenants; local integration tests show smoother transitions and reduced oscillation.
2026-03-14: Canary rollout plan approved by SRE; PR for canary config prepared and under review (see related_prs).
